key_insight: Off-the-shelf large language models can automatically abstract many key breast oncology variables from very long longitudinal charts with high agreement to expert review.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce manual chart-review burden in cancer research and make retrospective data extraction faster and more scalable, while still needing careful validation before broader use.
method: Open-source pipeline used general-purpose LLMs without fine-tuning or manual document selection.
Tested on 100 randomly selected breast cancer patients with long records and compared outputs against oncologist abstraction and other records.
A separate 97-patient cohort was used to check recurrence detection performance.
evidence_signal: In the best models, GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro, the pipeline reached 90%-100% concordance for several key variables and outperformed research coordinators on recurrence and therapy-line tasks.
watch_item: Performance was lower for therapy-line reconstruction, and the approach still requires replication and validation across institutions, cohorts, and diseases.
paper_title: Fully Automated Abstraction of Longitudinal Breast Oncology Records with Off-The-Shelf Large Language Models
